title: Assistant Professor of Economics - Macroeconomics
description:
Assistant Professor of Economics - Macroeconomics

Wayne State University is searching for an experienced Assistant
Professor of Economics - Macroeconomics at its Detroit campus
location.

Wayne State is a premier, public, urban research university located
in the heart of Detroit, Michigan where students from all
backgrounds are offered a rich, high-quality education. Our
deep-rooted commitment to excellence, collaboration, integrity,
diversity and inclusion creates exceptional educational
opportunities which prepare students for success in a global
society.

Essential functions (job duties):

The Department of Economics at Wayne State University invites
applications for a tenure-track position at the rank of Assistant
Professor, beginning on or about August 18, 2027. This is a
full-time (9-month), benefits-eligible faculty position.

The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to teaching
in macroeconomics and econometrics at both the undergraduate and
graduate levels. The Department offers B.A., M.A., and Ph.D.
programs. Candidates should demonstrate a strong commitment to
excellence in both research and teaching and should contribute to
the academic and professional activities of the department. The
teaching load is 2:2 (fall: winter semesters).

WSU is classified by the Carnegie Foundation as a RU/VH (Research
University, Very High research activity) institution and serves
more than 24,000 students across 370 academic programs, making it a
premier, public, urban research university located in the heart of
Detroit.

Qualifications:

We seek candidates specializing in macroeconomics with a strong
background in applied macroeconometrics.

Candidates should have an active research agenda in macroeconomics
and demonstrate strong potential for high-quality research and
publication.

Candidates are expected to hold a Ph.D. in Economics no later than
August 17, 2027.

To apply, go to https://jobs.wayne.edu. An on-line application is
required. Candidates must upload a cover letter, curriculum vitae,
job market paper, research statement, teaching statement, and
evidence of teaching effectiveness (teaching evaluations, if
available).

Three letters of recommendation should be sent to Liang Hu,
Department Chair, lianghu@wayne.edu, and Young-Ro Yoon, Chair of
the Search Committee, Department of Economics,
ed7847@wayne.edu

To receive full consideration, applications must be received by
November 16, 2026.
